feature1.prompt: RenameIndex() crashes when unnamed index is moving backward and forward. RenameIndex() should restore the old auto-generated name when an unnamed index for unique_together is migrating backward. The fix requires that when the old index name matches the new index name, the renaming operation should be skipped so that no unnecessary work is performed. This is meant to prevent crashes such as django.db.utils.ProgrammingError: relation "new_pony_test_idx" already exists, a problem especially seen on PostgreSQL. After the fix, re-applying RenameIndex() when the index names are identical should simply have no effect on the database state.
feature1.hint_texts: Modify the file django/db/migrations/operations/models.py in the database_forwards method of the RenameIndex operation. Insert a conditional check immediately after retrieving the old index so that if old_index.name is equal to the new name, the method returns early without executing further operations. This change ensures that the operation becomes idempotent when no renaming is required.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py, inside the function database_forwards of the RenameIndex operation. Start changes around the block where the old index is retrieved and compare old_index.name with self.new_name to decide whether to proceed.

feature2.prompt: Ensure that the RenameIndex() operation is validated to prevent crashes when re-applying the operation on an unnamed index. When the index names remain unchanged, re-applying the RenameIndex() should not attempt a redundant rename, thereby avoiding errors related to duplicate index creation. This feature focuses on verifying that the migration process retains the original auto-generated index name without triggering a crash. The expected behavior is that the system completes the migration without raising errors such as django.db.utils.ProgrammingError due to an already existing index.
feature2.hint_texts: Update the test in tests/migrations/test_operations.py to verify that the RenameIndex operation becomes a no-op when old and new index names are identical. Modify the test case test_rename_index_unnamed_index so that it re-applies the database_forwards method and asserts that the index name remains unchanged. This will involve adding an extra block in the test to run the operation a second time and then confirming the expected outcome.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/migrations/test_operations.py, in the function test_rename_index_unnamed_index. Begin changes by incorporating an additional schema_editor context that re-invokes the database_forwards method and checks that the index still exists with its expected name.

--- a/tests/migrations/test_operations.py
+++ b/tests/migrations/test_operations.py
@@ -2988,6 +2988,11 @@ def test_rename_index_unnamed_index(self):
         with connection.schema_editor() as editor, self.assertNumQueries(0):
             operation.database_backwards(app_label, editor, new_state, project_state)
         self.assertIndexNameExists(table_name, "new_pony_test_idx")
+        # Reapply, RenameIndex operation is a noop when the old and new name
+        # match.
+        with connection.schema_editor() as editor:
+            operation.database_forwards(app_label, editor, new_state, project_state)
+        self.assertIndexNameExists(table_name, "new_pony_test_idx")
         # Deconstruction.
         definition = operation.deconstruct()
         self.assertEqual(definition[0], "RenameIndex")
